ENGINEERING GUIDE

Vertical vs Horizontal Anodizing Lines

A practical decision guide for comparing anodizing line configurations using profiles, capacity, building constraints and process requirements.

PROJECT PLANNING / DAIMENG TECHNOLOGY

Choose the configuration after you understand the product mix, process route and factory constraints. A useful comparison begins with the same production assumptions for both options.

1. Describe the workpiece envelope

List the shortest and longest profiles, representative cross-sections, weights and the share of production each family represents. Include occasional products that the new line must accommodate. A nominal maximum size alone does not describe a factory’s production mix.

2. Review the building before the layout

Record usable floor space, clear internal height, columns, access openings and equipment maintenance areas. Vertical and horizontal handling arrangements create different layout questions. Ask for drawings that show loading, transfer and service space rather than just the process tanks.

3. Compare on the same capacity basis

Define output using agreed operating hours, loading assumptions and finish mix. Tonnes alone may hide differences in surface area and processing time. Ask how each proposal accounts for product changes, planned downtime and the slowest stage of the route.

4. Specify the finish mix

Identify required appearances, film thicknesses and acceptance criteria. Include any planned coloring or downstream coating. A line optimized around a single route should be compared differently from one expected to handle frequent changes.

5. Make the decision traceable

Build a comparison matrix with your team. Include building modifications, equipment scope, utility interfaces, operator tasks and the data required from the control system. Record every assumption that could change the result.

The line selector provides a discussion starting point. Final selection needs a project-specific engineering review.
